Policy Name: Cigna Lumbar Fusion (CMM-609: Lumbar Fusion with Decompression)
Referred Sections: CMM-609.8: Repeat Lumbar Fusion (Arthrodesis) at the Same Level

Required findings: Greater than six (6) months elapsed since the prior lumbar fusion
Daily pain of clinically significant intensity causing functional impairment (e.g., inability to perform household chores, inability to stand for prolonged periods)
Physical examination findings that are concordant with the reported symptoms

Failure of BOTH (unless contraindicated): prescription‑strength analgesics, steroids, gabapentinoids, and/or NSAIDs for at least six (6) weeks AND a provider‑directed exercise/physical‑therapy program for at least six (6) weeks
Post‑operative imaging performed no earlier than six (6) months after the prior fusion that demonstrates pseudoarthrosis at the requested level(s)
Post‑operative MRI or CT that correlates with the patient’s symptoms and confirms lack of solid fusion
Absence of unmanaged significant mental or behavioral health disorders (e.g., major depressive disorder, chronic pain syndrome, opioid use disorder)

Documentation of nicotine‑free status – either a never‑smoker declaration or abstinence from all tobacco/nicotine products for ≥6 weeks prior to planned surgery verified by an objective cotinine test (serum, urine, or saliva) within normal range
Medical necessity indications.Source: CMM-609.8: Repeat Lumbar Fusion (Arthrodesis) at the Same Level > Symptomatic Pseudoarthrosis

Non-Indications: Less than six (6) months since the prior lumbar fusion
Pain that is not daily or does not cause clinically significant functional limitation
Physical exam not concordant with reported symptoms
Imaging does not demonstrate pseudoarthrosis at the level(s) in question
Failure to complete the required six‑week trial of both appropriate pharmacologic therapy and a supervised exercise program (unless medically contraindicated)
Presence of unmanaged significant mental or behavioral health disorder
Active tobacco use without documented cessation or without a qualifying cotinine test
Cotinine test result outside the normal range or performed outside the six‑week pre‑operative window
Important criteria & exceptions: Both a six‑week course of prescription‑strength analgesics/NSAIDs/ gabapentinoids/steroids AND a six‑week supervised exercise program are required unless the patient has a documented contraindication to either therapy

Nicotine abstinence can be satisfied by a never‑smoker statement or by objective cotinine testing (serum, urine, or saliva) performed within six weeks of the planned surgery and reported as within normal limits
Mental/behavioral health disorders must be addressed and documented as stable or managed before surgery
Imaging must be obtained at least six months post‑operatively to reliably assess for pseudoarthrosis
Documentation required: Operative report from the prior lumbar fusion surgery
Post‑operative plain radiographs (including flexion‑extension views) or CT performed ≥6 months after the index fusion showing pseudoarthrosis
MRI or CT report confirming pseudoarthrosis and correlating with the patient’s symptoms
Comprehensive physical examination note documenting pain location, severity, neurologic findings, and functional limitation
Pain assessment documentation (e.g., pain diary, VAS scores) demonstrating daily pain with functional impairment
Medication records showing ≥6 weeks of prescription‑strength analgesics, steroids, gabapentinoids, and/or NSAIDs
Physical therapy or supervised exercise program records confirming ≥6 weeks of provider‑directed therapy
Behavioral health evaluation note confirming no unmanaged significant mental or behavioral health disorder
Smoking status documentation: either a signed never‑smoker statement or a cotinine test result (serum, urine, or saliva) performed within 6 weeks of surgery and reported as within normal range
Any prior imaging studies that establish the timeline of fusion and the development of pseudoarthrosis
